page.title: AI Simplified — Pranav PT
page.description: What is AI really? Understand machine learning, large language models, and AI tools — explained simply through real-world analogies.

sections.headline: AI is not magic. It's math that learned from examples.
sections.subheadline: Once you understand the core idea, every AI tool — ChatGPT, image generators, recommendation systems — suddenly makes sense.

sections.title: What is AI — in one analogy?
sections.body: Imagine you want to teach a child to recognize a dog. You don't give them a rulebook. You show them 10,000 photos — dog, not dog, dog, not dog. Eventually they just know. AI works the same way. Show it enough examples, and it learns the pattern. That's it. That's the core idea behind all of it.

visual.description: Simple diagram: pile of examples → pattern recognition → output

cards.title: Machine Learning
cards.description: Teaching computers to learn from data instead of following hardcoded rules.

cards.title: Large Language Models
cards.description: The technology behind ChatGPT. Trained on billions of sentences to predict the next word — extraordinarily well.

cards.title: Training
cards.description: The process of showing an AI millions of examples so it can learn patterns.

cards.title: Inference
cards.description: When you actually use an AI — asking it a question or generating an image. This is inference.

cards.title: Neural Networks
cards.description: The math structure loosely inspired by the brain that most modern AI is built on.

cards.title: Hallucination
cards.description: When AI confidently says something wrong. It doesn't know — it predicts. That's the difference.

items.explanation: A large language model that predicts the most useful next word based on your input and billions of training examples.
A model trained on what millions of users watched next, predicting what you'll enjoy based on your pattern.
A small language model trained on email replies to suggest short, relevant responses.
An image classification model trained on millions of face photos to identify the same person across images.
